title: Ministry of Finance Committee of Supply debate on fiscal stewardship, tax thresholds and procurement
what_it_is: A Committee of Supply debate on Head M (Ministry of Finance), where MPs moved cuts to the allocation and ministers responded on fiscal policy, tax, procurement and business support.
why_it_matters: The record sets out changes for businesses: Tender Lite for ICT procurement will launch from April 2026, and all GST-registered businesses must submit digital invoices via InvoiceNow by April 2031. For individuals, the Minister said the $20,000 personal income tax exemption threshold will be regularly reviewed, and the GST display concession for F&B and hotels will be reviewed in future. The amendment to reduce Head M by $100 was withdrawn.

key_points.point: Moved an amendment to reduce the total sum allocated for Head M of the Estimates by $100.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: That the total sum to be allocated for Head M of the Estimates be reduced by $100.

key_points.point: Raised the long-standing provision exempting the first $20,000 of chargeable income from tax and called for periodic review of structural thresholds.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: the long-standing provision that effectively exempts the first $20,000 of chargeable income from tax

key_points.point: Noted that the Prime Minister had said MOF will look into the $20,000 threshold.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: The Prime Minister already mentioned in his round-up speech that MOF will be looking into it.

key_points.point: Proposed three pathways for managing national capital: strategic investing in global norms, hunting as a pack, and placing Singaporeans overseas.
key_points.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
key_points.quote: I propose three pathways.

key_points.point: Raised a constituent retiree whose owner-occupied property tax is set by comparable rentals, including a neighbour's rental yield, and suggested capital value instead.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Under the Annual Value (AV) system, his property tax is set by comparable rentals, including his neighbour's.

key_points.point: Urged IRAS to conduct a public feedback exercise on displaying GST-inclusive prices and on the cost to hotels and restaurants of changing menus and ordering systems.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: I urge IRAS to conduct a proper public feedback exercise.

key_points.point: Asked how the Government balances replenishing reserves and supporting SME transformation, and how fiscal decisions preserve policy flexibility for future businesses.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
key_points.quote: I would like to ask the Minister to clarify two points.

key_points.point: Asked whether the Government will review rules across industries and verticals to increase operational flexibility and shorten processing times.
key_points.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
key_points.quote: I therefore ask whether the Government will undertake a review of rules across industries and verticals

key_points.point: Suggested a $2,500 tax credit comprising $1,500 for an NSman and $1,000 for a caregiver instead of tax relief.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
key_points.quote: I suggest a modest $2,500 tax credit, comprising $1,500 for an NSman and $1,000 for a caregiver instead of tax relief.

key_points.point: Suggested a GovAI Enterprise Assistant to give companies bespoke recommendations on tenders, grants and policy changes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
key_points.quote: GovAI Enterprise Assistant

key_points.point: Proposed three refinements for inclusive procurement: faster payments, smarter contract packaging, and recognising social value in contracts.
key_points.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
key_points.quote: MOF can better support SMEs with three refinements.

key_points.point: Proposed refreshing the Government Electronic Business System (GeBIZ) to streamline documentation and reduce repetitive submissions.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
key_points.quote: I propose that we refresh the Government Electronic Business System (GeBIZ)

key_points.point: Asked for an update on expanding TenderLite to infocomm technology contracts.
key_points.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
key_points.quote: I would like to ask for an update on the expansion of the TenderLite to infocomm technology (ICT) contracts.

key_points.point: Asked whether there is scope for stronger shared support, such as pooled investment platforms or enhanced central advisory capabilities, for Statutory Boards.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
key_points.quote: Is there scope for a stronger shared support, for example, pool investment platforms or enhanced central advisory capabilities

key_points.point: Suggested more frequent Progressive Wage Credit Scheme payouts, such as quarterly disbursements aligned with GST cycles.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
key_points.quote: more frequent payouts, such as quarterly disbursements aligned with GST cycles, would ease cash flow without increasing overall fiscal requirements.

key_points.point: Set out fiscal principles including fiscal prudence and sustainability, value for money, and finance as a catalyst.
key_points.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: First, fiscal prudence and sustainability.

key_points.point: Reported that in 2025 Government agencies with MOF and the Development Projects Advisory Panel achieved at least $1.4 billion in development cost avoidance.
key_points.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: In 2025, Government agencies, working together with MOF and DPAP, were able to achieve a total cost avoidance of at least $1.4 billion in development costs.

key_points.point: Said the same valuation basis should apply to all residential properties, whether owner-occupied, rented out or vacant.
key_points.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: One should adopt the same valuation basis for all residential properties, regardless of whether it is owner-occupied, rented out or vacant.

key_points.point: Said sales data is appropriate where there is a sale of land or property, including state land sales to HDB.
key_points.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: Sales data is appropriate for use where there is a sale of land or property, as sales data would be more directly relevant.

key_points.point: Said Customs is considering extending the validity period of certain licences from three years to five years.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: Customs is considering extending the validity period of certain licences from three years to five years

key_points.point: Said the GST display concession for F&B establishments and hotels will be reviewed in future, taking into account technology and business and consumer preferences.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: Nonetheless, we will review this in the future, to take into account technological improvements as well as business and consumer preferences.

key_points.point: Said MOM annualises Progressive Wage Credit Scheme payouts because wages in Progressive Wage Model sectors can vary throughout the year.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: MOM annualises Progressive Wage Credit Scheme payouts because the wages of workers in the Progressive Wage Model sectors can vary throughout the year.

key_points.point: Said Singapore is exploring ASEAN Single Window 2.0 to strengthen interoperability and expand electronic trade document exchanges to partners such as China, Japan and South Korea.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: We are now exploring ASEAN Single Window 2.0, to strengthen interoperability and to expand electronic trade-related document exchanges to partners, such as China, Japan and South Korea

key_points.point: Announced that all GST-registered businesses will be required to submit digital invoices to IRAS via InvoiceNow by April 2031.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: We will require all GST-registered businesses to submit digital invoices to IRAS via InvoiceNow by April 2031.

key_points.point: Said the income tax system will be regularly reviewed to ensure it is progressive and resilient.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: we will regularly review our income tax system to ensure that it is progressive and resilient

key_points.point: Said cash grants and credits are administratively simpler and more progressive than tax credits tied to payable taxes.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: Cash grants and credits are administratively simpler and more progressive than tax credits which are tied to payable taxes.

key_points.point: Said Temasek's mandate is to deliver good, sustainable long-term returns and that the Government does not prescribe specific investment areas.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: Temasek's mandate is to deliver good, sustainable long-term returns.

key_points.point: Announced MOF will launch Tender Lite for ICT procurement from April 2026.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
key_points.quote: MOF will be launching Tender Lite for ICT procurement from April 2026.

key_points.point: Said established track records are not a requirement for the Innovative Procurement Partnership, to make it more accessible to SMEs and startups.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
key_points.quote: established track records are not a requirement.

key_points.point: Said MOF will tap on the latest technology to comprehensively refresh the GeBIZ system.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
key_points.quote: we will tap on the latest technology to comprehensively refresh GeBIZ system.

key_points.point: Said MOF trialled AI on top of data analytics to obtain insights from large volumes of data for finance and audit.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
key_points.quote: we trialled the use of AI, on top of data analytics, to obtain insights from large volumes of data.

key_points.point: Asked what determines nominality for a service charge under the GST display concession.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: what determines nominality, if that is the standard for qualifying for concession?

key_points.point: Said IRAS takes a firm stance against businesses levying nominal service charges without genuine reason other than to avoid displaying GST-inclusive prices.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
key_points.quote: IRAS takes a firm stance against businesses who levy nominal service charges without genuine reason, other than to avoid displaying GST inclusive prices.

key_points.point: Asked whether MOF would consider extending AI subscription tools for businesses in the same spirit as for individuals.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
key_points.quote: whether MOF would consider extending AI subscription tools for businesses in the same spirit as for individuals.

key_points.point: Said MOF is working with GovTech to study AI tools that can be used within Statutory Boards, agencies and Ministries, and if useful, open them for businesses.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
key_points.quote: we are working with the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) to study what are some of the AI tools that can be used within the Statutory Boards, agencies and Ministries.

key_points.point: Withdrew his amendment to reduce the Head M allocation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
key_points.quote: I seek to leave to withdraw my amendment.

what_happens_next: Mr Saktiandi Supaat withdrew his amendment. MOF will launch Tender Lite for ICT procurement from April 2026; all GST-registered businesses must submit digital invoices via InvoiceNow by April 2031; ACRA will consult later this year; IRAS and IMDA will release more details on the InvoiceNow timeline and support; and the GST display concession will be reviewed in future.

Will the GST display concession for F&B establishments and hotels be changed, and on what timeline?
What standard will determine whether a service charge is nominal for the GST display concession?
Will tax credits for NSmen and caregivers be introduced?
Will owner-occupied property tax valuation move to capital value?
Will Progressive Wage Credit Scheme payouts become more frequent?
Will AI subscription support for businesses be introduced?
What are the detailed timeline and support measures for the mandatory InvoiceNow submission by April 2031?
Will Statutory Boards receive pooled investment platforms or enhanced central advisory capabilities?
Will the Government undertake a review of rules across industries and verticals to increase operational flexibility and shorten processing times?
